score_method: Minimum mandatory visual-area score, not an average; every mandatory static visual check must pass strictly above 9.0.
pending_separate_evidence: Full GitHub byte/blob readback and independent archive gate
preservation: All previous source identities, original accepted images, rejected iterations and exact prompts remain preserved.

areas.finding: The source-specific Giant Boar keeps the massive dark-brown body, tall swept-back shoulder mane, ridged broad snout and oversized pale side tusks, distinct from the ordinary Boar and older red Tusk Boar.
All six required cardinal/oblique views are distinct, labeled and fully framed. The front and rear obliques resolve limb, tusk, mane and tail attachments.

Four thick legs terminate in broad split hoof masses. The two main hoof halves and central clefts remain readable in the front, side and closeup evidence; smaller lateral rounded forms read as stylized dewclaws rather than additional broad central toes. All feet are grounded.
One large curved tusk emerges from each side of the mouth, with no extra horn. Ridged snout, two ears, smaller mouth teeth and a controlled snarl remain coherent across views.
One narrow tufted tail originates at the rump and is resolved in both profiles, rear and rear oblique. No extra tail or detached tuft is present.
Tall swept mane follows the shoulders and back; darker lower legs and major warm-brown fur masses remain stable through the rotation.
Polished sculpted fur, powerful rounded masses, legible labels, complete margins and soft ground shadows meet the source-guided static-reference standard.

source_interpretation_limit: The small original Atlas source fixes visible identity. Hidden reverse anatomy and fine surface construction are authored static-reference interpretation. This approval establishes no native mesh, rig, animation, use state or gameplay behavior.
minor_polish_limit: Hoof side/dewclaw shapes are chunky and stylized; a future native model should explicitly resolve principal hoof and dewclaw topology. This sheet establishes the paired split-hoof appearance, not a zoologically measured mesh. Fine mane tips vary slightly between illustrated views.
